title: FBISE Section A Board Examination Simulator 06 (FBISE Past Papers Focus I)
subject: english-10

questions.question: The father said to his son, "Do not waste your time." Choose the correct indirect speech:

options.A: The father forbade his son not to waste his time.
options.B: The father advised his son not to waste his time.
options.C: The father ordered his son to not waste your time.
options.D: The father told to his son do not waste his time.

questions.explanation: Negative imperative sentences are converted into 'advised/warned [object] not to [infinitive]'. Note: using 'forbade' already carries negative meaning so it cannot be followed by 'not'.

questions.question: Choose the correct passive voice: 'Who broke this mirror?'

options.A: By whom was this mirror broken?
options.B: By who was this mirror broken?
options.D: By whom this mirror was broken?

questions.explanation: Interrogative sentences with 'Who' change to 'By whom + auxiliary verb + subject + past participle' ('By whom was this mirror broken?').

questions.question: Choose the correct verb: 'A pair of shoes ___ kept under the stairs.'
questions.explanation: While 'shoes' is plural, the head noun of the subject phrase is the singular 'A pair', requiring the singular verb 'is'.

questions.question: Identify the underlined verbal: 'Seeing is *believing*.'
questions.explanation: 'Believing' follows the linking verb 'is' and renames/completes the subject 'Seeing', functioning as a subject complement gerund.

questions.question: Identify the underlined clause: 'You will not succeed *unless you persevere*.'
questions.explanation: 'unless you persevere' sets the prerequisite condition under which success occurs, making it an Adverb Clause of Condition.

questions.question: Identify the conditional: 'If plants do not receive sunlight, they die.'
questions.explanation: This expresses a biological universal truth; both the conditional clause and the main clause are in the present simple, marking a Zero Conditional.

questions.question: Choose the correct comparative form: 'Mount Everest is ___ than any other peak on Earth.'
questions.explanation: Comparison between two entities ('Mount Everest' vs 'any other peak') signaled by 'than' requires the comparative degree 'higher'.

questions.question: Identify the sentence type by purpose/meaning: 'Please close the front gate when leaving.'
questions.explanation: A sentence that makes a polite request, command, or instruction with an implied subject 'you' is an Imperative Sentence.

questions.question: Choose the appropriate preposition: 'The committee agreed ___ my proposed plan.'
questions.explanation: One agrees 'with' a person, but agrees 'to' a proposal, suggestion, or plan.

questions.question: What does the sunshine symbolize in the second stanza of 'The Rain'?

options.A: Universal equality, hope, and divine benevolence

questions.explanation: The bright sunshine that illuminates every dark droplet equally symbolizes a hopeful, egalitarian society free of socioeconomic disparity.

questions.question: The mother said to her son, "May you succeed in life!" Choose the correct indirect speech:

options.A: The mother wished that her son may succeed in life.
options.B: The mother prayed that her son might succeed in life.
options.C: The mother prayed her son would succeed in life.
options.D: The mother exclaims that her son might succeed in life.

questions.explanation: In optative sentences expressing a prayer or benediction, the reporting verb changes to 'prayed', connector 'that' is used, and 'may' shifts to 'might'.

questions.question: Select the correct passive voice: 'Why did you punish him?'

options.A: Why was he punished by you?
options.B: Why did he be punished by you?
options.C: Why he was punished by you?
options.D: Why had he been punished by you?

questions.explanation: In past simple interrogative passive, 'Why did you punish him?' becomes 'Why was he punished by you?' maintaining inversion (auxiliary 'was' before subject 'he').

questions.explanation: 'Polished' transfers action directly to the object 'the table', which makes it a transitive verb.

questions.question: Which of the following verbs is followed by a BARE INFINITIVE without 'to'?
questions.explanation: The verb 'let' takes a bare infinitive (e.g., 'Let him go', not 'Let him to go').

questions.question: Identify the underlined clause: '*Although he was exhausted*, he completed the marathon.'
questions.explanation: 'Although he was exhausted' introduces an acknowledged contrast or concession, making it an Adverb Clause of Concession.
